matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When trying to fix the equation, first attempt to move a single matchstick within the same character, as many valid transformations involve only reshaping a single symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Apply this before considering moves that involve two different characters.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from one numeral to another, leaving the original character with a single diagonal stick (invalid).

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, check that each resulting character corresponds to a valid Roman numeral or allowed operator; an invalid shape (e.g., a lone diagonal) invalidates the solution.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any stick relocation, before evaluating arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from X leaves a lone diagonal, which is not a recognized numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A solitary diagonal stick does not represent any Roman numeral; ensure that removing a diagonal from V or X does not leave an isolated diagonal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering removing a diagonal from a numeral, verify that the remaining shape is still a valid numeral.
matchstick.example: Taking one diagonal from V and not adding it elsewhere, resulting in a single diagonal stick.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If no intra-character move yields a valid equation, explore moving a stick from one character to a different character, ensuring both source and target remain valid.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I to the plus sign without checking that the plus remains a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation after any transformation; the equality must hold for the solution to be correct.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After confirming symbol validity, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '-' but not checking that 16 = 16 - 16 is false.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign after stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If a stick is taken from the '=' sign, ensure the remaining symbol still forms a valid equality sign (i.e., two horizontal sticks); otherwise the equation is invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a stick from the equals sign.
matchstick.example: Removing one horizontal from '=' leaves a single '-' sign, breaking the equality.

matchstick.title: Validate whole numeral strings for proper Roman numeral syntax
matchstick.principle: After any stick move, verify that each multi-character numeral follows standard Roman numeral ordering rules (e.g., no 'IXIV' or repeated V).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After confirming individual symbols, before arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Creating 'IXIV' by moving a stick, which is not a standard Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Intra-character diagonal transformation (V↔X)
matchstick.principle: When a character is V or X (both composed of two diagonal sticks), moving one diagonal within the same character can change V to X or vice versa; consider this before inter‑character moves.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During intra-character exploration, especially when V or X appear.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X and leaving a single diagonal, instead of repositioning it to form V.

matchstick.title: Transform '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick to an adjacent I
matchstick.principle: If a '+' operator and an adjacent 'I' numeral are present, moving the vertical stick from '+' to the 'I' can turn '+' into '-' and the 'I' into 'II', potentially fixing the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a '+' next to an 'I' and a simple arithmetic adjustment is needed.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical from '+' to an 'I' but forgetting to update the arithmetic, leading to a false equality.

matchstick.title: Intra-character operator transformation (e.g., '+' → '=', '-' → '=') by rotating a stick within the same operator
matchstick.principle: Operators can be changed by rotating a stick within the same character; for example, turning '+' into '=' by rotating its vertical stick to a horizontal orientation, or turning '-' into '=' by adding a horizontal from elsewhere. This counts as a single stick move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains '+' or '-' and a one‑stick transformation might resolve the equality, consider rotating or reorienting a stick within the operator before moving sticks between characters.
matchstick.example: Attempting to move the vertical stick from '+' to another character instead of rotating it within '+' to create '=', missing a valid solution.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to focus on moving sticks between characters, missing simpler changes that can be made by reshaping a single symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: First explore all possible intra‑character stick relocations, including rotating sticks within the same character, before considering inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Leaving a single angled stick after moving a diagonal from X or V (invalid numeral)
matchstick.why_it_happens: When a diagonal is removed from a V or X, the model forgets that a lone diagonal does not correspond to any Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After removing a diagonal, verify that the remaining shape forms a valid numeral; if not, either keep the diagonal or relocate it to create a valid character.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model often checks symbol validity but forgets to compute the numeric values to confirm the equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After confirming that all symbols are valid, always compute the values of both sides and ensure they are equal before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., converting '=' to '-' or vice versa) automatically solve the puzzle, without ensuring a single '=' remains
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats operator changes as independent of the overall equation structure, overlooking the requirement that exactly one '=' must stay.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Maintain exactly one equality sign; if an operator is changed, verify that the equation still contains a single '=' and that the arithmetic holds.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character operator transformations (e.g., '+' → '=', '-' → '=') and assuming operator changes require moving sticks between characters
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on moving sticks to other characters and does not consider rotating a stick within the same operator to change its shape.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When an operator is present, consider rotating or reorienting its sticks within the same character to produce a different valid operator before moving sticks elsewhere.
